title: Count Rotations With Exactly K Equal Adjacent Pairs
summary: Given a string s of length n and an integer k , count the number of cyclic rotations of s such that the score of each rotation equals k .
statement: Given a string s of length n and an integer k , count the number of cyclic rotations of s such that the score of each rotation equals k . The score of a rotation is defined as the number of indices i (where 0 ≤ i < n - 1 ) for which the characters at positions i and i + 1 are the same.
constraints: A cyclic rotation’s score counts equal adjacent pairs at ordinary indices 0..n-2; the wrap pair is not counted.
Return how many of the n rotations have score k.
hints: A rotation changes only the pair removed at one end and the pair introduced at the other.
The score can be updated in constant time per shift, or directly recomputed for clarity.
Count each of n shifts whose n-1 internal adjacent comparisons equal k.
Enumerating all shifts covers every cyclic rotation exactly once.
editorial: Enumerating all shifts covers every cyclic rotation exactly once.

tests.explanation: Two rotations contain exactly one equal adjacent pair.
All three rotations have no equal adjacent pair.
